/
艾兒是一名剛從甜點學校畢業的資優生，對美好的甜點師生涯抱有憧憬。

/
偶然遇見了傳說中的甜點師正在急徵同行。
雪。一名開著雙層巴士改裝的行動餐車，四處旅行。

！安排一場偶遇契機。

/
艾早就耳聞這位活傳說，簡直是求之不得的機會，立刻答應下來，卻沒想到，這根本形同同居生活。

！描繪雙層巴士的生活機能齊全，唯獨寢室的部分只有一組雙人床房間。

/
二人曖昧升溫，雪似乎不以為意，艾兒卻開始胡思亂想。

！雪與艾兒的設定、名字，請使用附件。
！雪：Icy
！艾兒：Arte
！請使用文字框，並且使用AI Cream規範，不要有對我說話的內容。

ChatGPT
Arte had graduated from pastry school at the top of her class, armed with excellent grades, an unreasonable amount of confidence, and a very clear picture of the career she wanted.

A proper pastry kitchen. A respected chef. Her own creations displayed behind spotless glass.

Preferably with people applauding her talent.

She had not, however, planned on finding her first real opportunity on the side of a highway.

The vehicle was impossible to miss.

It was a double-decker bus painted in soft, understated colors, with a serving window cut into the lower level and a handwritten sign propped beside it:

**Icy's Patisserie — Today: Somewhere.**

Arte stared at it.

"Somewhere?"

A woman stepped out from behind the serving window carrying a tray of freshly baked pastries.

She was tall, pale-haired, and composed enough to look completely out of place standing beside what was essentially a traveling bakery.

Icy glanced at the sign.

Then at the road.

Then back at the sign.

"Wrong place?"

Arte blinked.

"No. I'm looking for Icy."

"Oh."

The woman nodded.

"That's me."

Arte nearly dropped her portfolio.

It was *her*.

The legendary pastry chef who had apparently abandoned the idea of owning a permanent shop and instead turned a double-decker bus into a fully functional mobile kitchen.

Arte had read about her for years.

She had studied her recipes.

She had watched interviews.

She had even attempted one of Icy's signature desserts during her final exam.

And now the woman was standing three feet away from her, holding a tray of cream puffs as if this were the most ordinary thing in the world.

"I heard you're looking for an assistant."

"Yes."

"I'll do it."

Icy looked at her.

"Fast."

"I've been looking for you for twenty minutes."

"Still fast."

Arte folded her arms.

"I'm a pastry school graduate."

"I know."

That stopped her.

"...You know?"

"I saw your application."

Arte's eyebrows rose.

"You actually read it?"

"Yes."

"And?"

Icy considered this for a moment.

"Your handwriting is bad."

Arte's smile twitched.

"My *handwriting*?"

"But your desserts look good."

"...Thank you."

"You're hired."

That was how Arte's dream career began.

It also took approximately three hours for her to discover the catch.

The bus was not merely a food truck.

The lower floor contained a compact professional kitchen, storage cabinets, refrigeration, a washing station, and even a small dining area.

The upper floor was a completely functional living space.

A sitting room.

A tiny office.

A bathroom.

A shower.

A surprisingly well-equipped kitchenette.

A washing machine.

Everything was arranged with the efficiency of someone who had spent years living on the road.

Arte slowly looked around.

"This is... actually impressive."

Icy nodded.

"Mm."

"You live here?"

"Yes."

"Full-time?"

"Usually."

Arte looked toward the stairs.

"And where am I supposed to sleep?"

Icy pointed upstairs.

"Bedroom."

Arte followed her.

Then stopped.

There was one bedroom.

One.

And inside it was one bed.

A very comfortable-looking double bed.

Arte stared.

Icy stared at the bed.

Then at Arte.

Then back at the bed.

"Oh."

Arte's face heated instantly.

"'Oh'?!"

"There's only one."

"I can see that!"

Icy tilted her head.

"You want the sofa?"

Arte looked back downstairs.

The sofa was small.

Very small.

She looked at the bed again.

"...No."

"Okay."

Icy walked away.

Just like that.

Arte remained frozen in the doorway.

'Okay?!'

She had imagined her first job with Icy countless times.

Learning secret techniques.

Creating beautiful desserts.

Traveling across the country.

Maybe becoming a famous pastry chef herself.

She had never imagined sharing a bed with her.

Especially not on the first day.

And somehow, the worst part was that Icy didn't seem bothered in the slightest.

That woman was either unbelievably calm...

Or completely oblivious.

Probably both.

The first night, Arte lay rigidly on one side of the bed, staring at the ceiling.

Beside her, Icy was already asleep.

Or at least appeared to be.

Arte carefully shifted an inch away.

The mattress moved.

Icy's eyes opened.

"Cold?"

"No."

"Then?"

"Nothing."

"Okay."

Her eyes closed again.

Arte stared at her profile in the dim light.

'How can she be this relaxed?'

Another inch.

Icy's hand suddenly reached across the mattress and caught the edge of Arte's blanket.

She pulled it back over Arte's shoulder.

"You're uncovered."

Arte went completely still.

"...Thanks."

"Mm."

Icy went back to sleep.

Arte's heart did not.

This was going to be a problem.

A very serious problem.

Because the longer they traveled together, the more Arte began noticing things she absolutely did not need to notice.

The way Icy always remembered exactly how much sugar she preferred in her coffee.

The way she silently left the warmer side of the bed to Arte whenever the nights became cold.

The way Icy would casually lean against her while reading recipes, apparently unaware that their shoulders were touching.

The way she sometimes looked at Arte for a second too long.

Or maybe Arte was imagining that.

Probably imagining it.

Definitely imagining it.

One afternoon, Arte was decorating a batch of miniature fruit tarts when Icy appeared beside her.

She leaned over the counter.

"Pretty."

Arte glanced sideways.

"The tarts?"

"Yes."

A pause.

"...Obviously."

Icy looked at her.

"Your face too."

Arte froze.

The piping bag in her hand stopped moving.

Icy reached over, calmly picked up one of the finished tarts, and walked away.

"Good work."

Arte stared after her.

Her cheeks slowly turned pink.

'She did that on purpose.'

There was no other explanation.

The woman was a menace.

A beautiful, emotionally unreadable, completely shameless menace.

Arte looked down at the ruined cream decoration beneath her piping tip.

"...I hate this job."

From the other side of the bus came Icy's voice.

"No, you don't."

Arte's face became even hotter.

She hated that Icy was right.

ChatGPT
That first night, Arte's thoughts refused to settle.

She had never been confused about liking women. Not once. It was simply part of who she was, something she had always been comfortable with—and even proud of.

And if she was being completely honest, her admiration for Icy had never been entirely innocent.

There had always been another kind of attraction mixed in with the professional awe.

She just hadn't expected to be sleeping beside the woman herself.

'This is so embarrassing.'

What if Icy didn't know?

What if she found out?

Wouldn't it be incredibly rude to lie there beside someone while secretly thinking about her like that?

Arte curled herself toward the very edge of the mattress, putting as much distance between them as physically possible.

There.

Safe.

She kept her back to Icy and pulled the blanket almost up to her chin.

'Just sleep.'

Easy.

She could do that.

Except the mattress shifted behind her.

Arte froze.

She waited.

Nothing.

Maybe Icy had simply turned over.

Good.

Then, sometime later, something warm settled against her back.

An arm.

Arte's eyes snapped open.

She didn't dare move.

Icy had apparently rolled toward her in her sleep, one arm resting loosely around Arte's waist.

Her body was close enough that Arte could feel the warmth of her through the blanket.

And then came the final blow.

A soft breath brushed the back of Arte's neck.

Once.

Then again.

Slow, warm, completely unconscious.

Arte's entire body went rigid.

'No.'

She stared into the darkness.

'No, no, no.'

Icy shifted slightly closer, apparently searching for a comfortable position without ever waking.

Her forehead nearly touched the back of Arte's head.

Another warm breath slipped over Arte's neck.

Arte clutched the blanket.

Her heart was pounding so loudly she was convinced Icy had to hear it.

'She's asleep.'

That was the only thing keeping Arte from completely losing her mind.

Icy didn't know.

She wasn't doing this on purpose.

She was just asleep.

Completely innocent.

Arte swallowed.

Very carefully, she tried to inch forward.

Icy's arm tightened around her instead.

Arte stopped breathing.

"..."

She stared helplessly at the wall.

This was impossible.

She had spent the entire evening worrying about accidentally making Icy uncomfortable.

Now Icy was the one holding her.

And somehow, that made everything ten times worse.

Arte squeezed her eyes shut.

'I'm going to die.'

Behind her, Icy remained peacefully asleep.

Arte, meanwhile, spent the rest of the night wide awake.

'Stay calm, Arte. Enjoy it.'

Wasn't this exactly what she'd dreamed about?

'...Wait. What am I even thinking?!'

Icy had no idea.

She had no idea Arte was lying there, desperately trying not to think about how much she wanted to be held by her.

The thought alone made Arte's face burn.

'I can't do this.'

She tried to pull away again.

Nothing.

Icy's arm remained around her like a surprisingly effective restraint.

Arte stared at the darkness, trapped in the embrace of the woman she had admired for years.

'This is torture.'

Eventually, fate took pity on her.

Icy shifted in her sleep, her arm loosening for just a moment.

Arte's eyes flew open.

Now.

She slipped out of the bed with the speed of someone escaping a crime scene, grabbed her pillow and blanket, and hurried downstairs.

The tiny sofa was barely large enough for one person.

She didn't care.

She curled herself up on it and closed her eyes.

'Much safer.'

It took her less than a minute to fall asleep.

---

The next morning, Arte woke to someone staring at her.

She opened one eye.

Icy was standing beside the sofa, looking genuinely puzzled.

Arte jolted upright.

Her face immediately turned bright red.

"You're awake."

"Y-Yeah..."

Icy glanced at the bed upstairs, then back at the tiny sofa.

"Bed uncomfortable?"

Arte froze.

"Too small?"

"No—"

"Do I sleep badly?"

"Not that either."

Icy's questions came one after another, short and completely matter-of-fact.

Arte's brain went into emergency mode.

'How am I supposed to explain this?!'

She couldn't exactly say:

*I escaped because you hugged me in your sleep and your breathing on my neck made me lose my mind.*

Absolutely not.

Her face burned hotter.

"I..."

Icy waited.

Arte looked away.

"...I'm on my period."

Silence.

Icy nodded.

"Oh."

She believed her.

Just like that.

Arte let out the tiniest breath of relief.

Crisis averted.

For now.

The rest of the day passed in a strange mixture of work and discovery.

Arte helped with the simpler tasks first, learning the quirks of Icy's equipment and the way everything had been arranged inside the bus.

The kitchen wasn't exactly spacious.

Even by the standards of a converted double-decker, the narrow aisles had been designed remarkably well. Every counter, shelf, oven, and storage compartment had its place.

There was very little wasted space.

Which also meant there was very little space to get out of someone's way.

Whenever Icy turned sideways to slip past Arte, their shoulders nearly brushed.

Every single time, Arte held her breath.

"Excuse me."

Icy's voice came from right beside her.

Arte immediately pressed herself against the counter.

"Go ahead."

Icy slipped past.

Her sleeve brushed Arte's arm.

Arte stared straight ahead until Icy had disappeared around the corner.

'Normal.'

She had to act normal.

This was just a kitchen.

People worked in kitchens together all the time.

There was absolutely no reason for her heart to react like that.

By the end of the day, most of what they ate consisted of their own baking experiments.

A slightly misshapen tart here.

An experimental cream filling there.

A batch of cookies that had come out better than expected.

It was, in many ways, exactly the life Arte had dreamed of.

Traveling with a legendary pastry chef.

Learning directly from her.

Spending her days surrounded by the smell of butter, sugar, and freshly baked pastry.

And yet, because of one tiny secret Arte couldn't bring herself to say aloud, she couldn't enjoy any of it quite as freely as she wanted.

That evening, when they finished cleaning up, Arte glanced toward the stairs.

Then toward the little sofa.

Maybe she could sleep there again.

It would be easier.

She had barely taken one step toward it when a hand caught her shoulder from behind.

"Upstairs."

Arte nearly jumped.

Icy had appeared behind her without a sound.

"I—"

Icy pointed toward the stairs.

"I put an extra blanket on the bed. Don't worry."

Arte stared at her.

"...You did?"

"Mm."

Icy released her shoulder and walked upstairs as though the matter were already settled.

Arte remained where she was.

There was no excuse this time.

No period.

No uncomfortable sofa.

No emergency escape route.

She slowly looked up at the stairs.

Then sighed.

"...Right."

She followed.

The awkward torture was back.

And this time, there was nowhere to run.
